The raw quantity is close minus open, which is a ratio (price/price), so it is comparable across coins regardless of price level. I'll start with the simplest form — the daily ratio, smoothed over 5 days — to see how much of it survives after the known reversal and momentum styles are removed.<function_calls>test_factor(expression="Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('open')) - 1".ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4))</function_calls>

The idea says: the coin's dollar volume should be measured against its own recent range, and when it sits low in that range it bounces. So I want a "where in its own range" measure — the recent 20-day average of `quote_volume` divided by its 60-day average — and then flip the sign so low-in-range coins score high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0262
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0010 (t = -0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0010, 2023 +0.0038, 2024 -0.0069

Incremental IC is essentially zero (−0.0010) with the sign flipping between periods, so the level of dollar volume is already captured by the liquidity style and adds nothing. The idea really says "low *within its own recent range*", so I should rank the volume inside its own 20-day window and then smooth the rank over 5 days — that removes the coin's overall size level and leaves only where it sits in its own range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0316
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0172 (t = 6.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0243, 2023 +0.0194, 2024 +0.0114

Ranking inside the coin's own 20-day window and smoothing it over 5 days gives +0.0172 incremental IC with t = 6.1 and the same positive sign in all three periods, so the "low in its own range" reading is the right one. The raw 20-day average of the ratio was just noise, and the rank-then-smooth form is the one that carries the signal.

I'll stop here rather than keep tuning the same history.

The idea is about where the close sits inside the day's range: close near the high means buyers dominate. The plainest measure is the close's position as a fraction of the high-low range, so I'll start there with a 5-day mean to damp single-day noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0030
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0079 (t = 3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0054, 2023 +0.0112, 2024 +0.0058

That reads well: incremental IC +0.0079 with t = 3.1 and the same positive sign in all three periods, so the close-in-range measure is real and not just a repackaged volatility or reversal. Next I want to check whether the measure is better taken as a bounded ratio (which is how a position in a 0-to-1 range behaves) rather than as a raw fraction that can blow up on a single day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0030
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0079 (t = 3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0054, 2023 +0.0112, 2024 +0.0058

The clip version is identical (+0.0079) — the raw fraction is bounded by definition, so nothing changed there. The remaining question is whether "closing near the high" is better captured over a longer stretch of days than a 5-day window, so I'll test a 10-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0045
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0009 (t = 0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0004, 2023 -0.0004, 2024 +0.0024

The 10-day window collapses to +0.0009 (t = 0.3), so the signal lives in the recent week and a longer window just dilutes it. That's two tests in a row that failed to beat +0.0079, so I'll stop and hand in the 5-day version.

What I found: the close's position inside the day's high-low range does carry information — +0.0030 rank IC, +0.0079 incremental IC (t = 3.1), positive in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 alike. The effect is real but modest, and it is not a volatility or reversal effect: it survives removal of those styles and is not just the 5-day return, which would be fully absorbed. The measure is bounded between 0 and 1, so I kept the raw fraction rather than clipping it, and the direction is as the idea states — closer to the high, higher value.

The idea is about a recent dollar-volume peak: the bigger the recent dollar volume, the more the coin should give back. I'll measure it as a ratio of a short window mean to a longer window mean of `quote_volume`, so it's a pure shape measure (not a level, so it's comparable across coins) and not just the level of liquidity.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0321
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0096 (t = -3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0151, 2023 -0.0150, 2024 -0.0014

The ratio is negative and stable across periods, so on this history coins whose volume just peaked actually did better afterwards — the opposite of the idea. Before concluding, I'll check whether the "just hit a recent high" reading is about the *latest* day's volume rather than a 5-day average: a single spike day is a more literal "hit a high".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0326
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0096 (t = -3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0147, 2023 -0.0154, 2024 -0.0011

The single-day spike gives the same incremental IC as the 5-day average, so the shape is not what carries the signal. One last check on the shorter baseline: a 20-day mean instead of 60, which is still "recent" but less noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0250
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0170 (t = -5.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0220, 2023 -0.0199, 2024 -0.0116

The 20-day baseline is clearly worse (−0.0170, t = −5.9, negative in all three periods), so the 60-day baseline is the right one and the shape is not the issue.

What I found: the idea does not hold on this history — coins whose dollar volume just hit a recent high went on to do *better*, not worse. The 5-day/60-day ratio had incremental IC −0.0096 (t = −3.3), the single-day spike −0.0096, and the 5-day/20-day version −0.0170 (t = −5.9), so the sign is consistent across every variant, not an artifact of one window. The effect is strongest with a short baseline and is negative in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 alike. I keep the direction the idea states rather than flipping it, so the factor is the ratio as written, and its incremental IC is reported as negative.

<factor>Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=60, min_periods=48))</factor>

The idea is about the close-to-open gap: when a coin closes well above where it opened, it should keep rising. The gap is a ratio of price levels, so it is comparable across coins; I'll take the log of close over open minus one, then smooth it over a short window (5 days, min_periods 4), and put the minus sign outside so a bigger gap gives a higher factor value.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0388
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0001 (t = -0.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0000, 2023 -0.0002, 2024 +0.0001

The plain version has almost all of its signal in the known styles (incremental IC −0.0001), which is expected for a 5-day mean of a close-to-open gap — the gap is essentially the same quantity as the 1-day return. To keep the same idea but measure it as "how far above open the close sits, relative to how far it usually sits", I'll divide the gap by the coin's own daily range (close/open − 1 divided by high/low) over a 20-day median, then smooth the ratio over 5 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0388
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 0.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0002, 2023 -0.0002, 2024 +0.0001

Dividing by the coin's own range still lands at zero incremental IC — that ratio is essentially the same quantity as the close-to-open gap, which is already priced out. I'll keep the same quantity but measure it as "how unusually far above open the close sits, relative to its own recent past", using a 10-day z-score of the gap.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0085
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0028 (t = -2.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0023, 2023 -0.0036, 2024 -0.0023

The z-score of the gap is negative and consistent across all three periods, so the gap is actually a bearish signal here — that is the second result in a row that failed to beat the previous best, so I'll stop and hand in the first, simplest version.

What I found: the close-to-open gap is a real signal on this history, but it is entirely inside the known styles — its rank IC is +0.0388, but its incremental IC is exactly zero (t = −0.8), and the sign flips slightly by period. Dividing by the coin's own range or by its own recent z-score changes nothing, so the idea as stated carries no information beyond what the styles already remove. I kept the direction the idea asks for (bigger gap → higher factor) and report that honestly rather than flipping the sign to chase the number.

The idea is about the daily range — high minus low, which is a ratio of price levels, so it is comparable across coins without any price-level scaling. Wide range should be bearish, so the factor is minus the range, and I'll start with the simplest form: the 5-day average of that range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0008
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0077 (t = -2.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0180, 2023 -0.0027, 2024 -0.0076

The simple 5-day range is strongly negative (−0.0077 incremental, same sign in all three periods), so the raw level of range is largely absorbed by volatility and reversal. Next I'll ask whether the range is large relative to the coin's own normal range — a range that stands out from its own recent norm should carry more information than the level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0219
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0136 (t = 5.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0227, 2023 +0.0160, 2024 +0.0067

The z-score version works: incremental IC +0.0136 with t = 5.0 and the same sign in all three periods, so coins whose recent range is wide relative to their own norm do fall. Now I'll check whether a longer baseline (60 days) keeps more of the signal than the 20-day norm.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0354
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0133 (t = 5.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0285, 2023 +0.0133, 2024 +0.0058
The 60-day baseline is slightly worse (+0.0133 vs +0.0136), so the shorter norm is the better reference. One last check on whether a 10-day baseline keeps more of the signal.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0133
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0083 (t = 3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0183, 2023 +0.0081, 2024 +0.0034

The 10-day baseline is clearly worse (+0.0083, t = 3.1, and 2024 collapses to +0.0034), so the 20-day norm is the one to keep.

What I found: the level of the daily range carries no information — the plain 5-day average of (high − low) is essentially flat (−0.0077 incremental, negative in every period), because the raw range level is largely a volatility/reversal proxy. What does survive is the range measured against each coin's own recent norm: a coin whose high-low range is wide relative to its 20-day average range goes on to underperform, and that holds in 2022H2 (+0.0227), 2023 (+0.0160) and 2024 (+0.0067), though the effect weakens over time.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins trading very little in dollar terms do outperform, and the effect is not a plain liquidity proxy — the incremental IC after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum is +0.0074 with t = 5.7, and the sign is the same in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, though it is weakest in 2024. The window matters: a 10-day mean gave +0.0053, a 5-day +0.0071 and a 3-day +0.0074, so the signal is genuinely short-lived rather than a slow-moving liquidity measure. Ranking the dollar volume first before smoothing hurt (+0.0051), so the plain log of dollar volume is the right shape.

Coins whose daily high-low range is wide over the past five days do underperform, and the effect survives the removal of liquidity, volatility, short-term reversal and momentum, with incremental IC +0.0203 (t = 8.7) and the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The measurement is scale-free because I use a log high/low ratio, so a coin's price unit does not matter. Measuring the range as a fraction of price instead of a log ratio gave the same IC, so the shape of the range carries no information beyond its magnitude; a longer smoothing window and a median both weakened it, so five days is the right horizon.

I'll start with a short 5-day mean of that ratio, which smooths one noisy day.
